prioritySignals.note: Migration branch: all touched files are new to master — history-based hotspot/bugfix signals are flat; testGaps computed as source files in the diff without a co-changing test file.

rawResults.suggestion: Replace the spurious Or with the canonical adjacency and all-distinct guards (pairwise Ne predicates or a DiffEq-style |a-b|!=1 form) and assert the case produces at least one answer line.
rawResults.description: search_dwelling's innermost guard is Predicate::Or(vec![Eq(smith,0), Eq(fletcher,0)]) — unsatisfiable on floors 1..=5, so case amb/03-multiple-dwelling yields zero answers. The conformance oracle shares this same Search program, so engine and reference agree on an empty transcript and the case certifies nothing. The fixture also drops the canonical all-distinct and |smith-fletcher|!=1 / |fletcher-cooper|!=1 adjacency constraints that the Kotlin/OCaml/TypeScript amb/03 fixtures implement (its own comment at line 764 claims 'all distinct' though no distinct predicate exists).

rawResults.suggestion: Capture mark = trail.len() before reference_bind (or pop until var's own trail entry inclusive) so the reference mirrors rollback_binding.
rawResults.description: reference_explore's ChooseRange/ChooseFrom loops call reference_rollback(trail, bindings, trail.len() - 1) after each body exploration, popping exactly the last trail entry instead of everything pushed since the variable's bind (the teaching engine's rollback_binding(var) at line 322 pops all entries since and including var's bind). Trailed Set writes inside a loop body therefore leak into later iterations of the reference model — a rollback-discipline divergence in the very property the amb/03 lesson note ('trailed assignment rollback') claims to check. Latent because no corpus Search program places a Set inside a ChooseRange/ChooseFrom body.

rawResults.suggestion: Give each case descriptor a minimal checkable expectation (answer count, or an expected-stdout hash) reviewed against the canonical case intent, or embed the real predicate program rather than its hand-picked answers.
rawResults.description: Rust experiment-case JSON descriptors carry only a constructor name, so fixture correctness exists only inside the binary: search_prime_sum encodes Or(SumEq(i+j,7), SumEq(i+j,11)) with a literal pair of 'taught primes' instead of the real primality predicate that Kotlin (isPrime over 1..4), OCaml (prime/prime_test), and TypeScript (isPrime over chosen lists) implement for the same amb/02-prime-sum-pair case. Engine and oracle share the constructor table, so a weaker or wrong program is conformance-invisible.

rawResults.suggestion: Give machine/04 its own monitored-print controller (or a distinct constructor + reference transcript emitting each remainder) so the case identity exercises the effect lesson.
rawResults.description: machine/01-gcd and machine/04-gcd-print both resolve to the same gcd_machine constructor with the same inputs (206/40), so the two case identities run literally the same program — the per-step perform-print lesson that OCaml (prints every remainder t) and Kotlin (prints every a) implement under 04-gcd-print collapses into a duplicate of 01 in the Rust suite. machine_reference hand-derives only the final answer, so nothing flags that the distinct lesson is uncovered.

rawResults.suggestion: Make MachineModel raise the same typed categories as Machine for unknown labels/instructions/ops, unassigned reads, and stack underflow (or share MachineScript's strict decode instead of re-lexing lines).
rawResults.description: MachineModel — the reference oracle for machine cases — silently defaults on every malformed-input class the grammar pins as typed errors (grammar.md:370-371 UnassignedRegister/ShapeFault): unknown instruction -> pc+1 (1143), goto/branch unknown label -> pc+1 (1129-1132), save/operand/sourceValue on an unassigned register -> 0L (1135/1190/1202), restore underflow -> 0L (1139), unknown test op -> false (1169), unknown perform op -> skipped (1181), unknown compute op -> left (1215). The teaching Machine raises UnassignedRegister/ShapeFault on the same conditions (Machine.kt:249/333/400/405/430), so the oracle fabricates deterministic-but-wrong observations instead of checking the error contract — duplicated-but-divergent machine semantics, invisible on the well-formed corpus.

rawResults.suggestion: Seed only const lines (leave declared registers VUnassigned), raise UnassignedRegister/ShapeFault on missing or mis-shaped operands, and render unassigned registers as a marker rather than 0.
rawResults.description: The teaching machine path silently defaults where grammar.md:477-478 pins 'Registers start unassigned; a read before any write raises UnassignedRegister': MachineScript.parse seeds every registers-line name to 0L (237-238) and machineEngine writes VLong(0) into each (168-170), so declared-but-unwritten registers read 0; const for an undeclared register is silently dropped (?: continue, 169); every op defaults missing args to VLong(0L) and asLong maps non-numeric operands to 0L (263-298) instead of ShapeFault — and 'rem' with one operand computes '% 0' as a raw ArithmeticException, violating 'engine implementations report the category, never raw host exceptions' (grammar:373); renderRegister renders non-numeric register content as "0" (186-194).

rawResults.suggestion: Escape every ch < 0x20 as \u%04x (matching the Rust driver) so the emitted observation stays valid JSON for arbitrary transcripts.
rawResults.description: Driver.escape omits control characters below 0x20 other than \n \r \t, so a transcript containing e.g. \u000b or NUL produces invalid JSON and the harness's one-object parse fails as a generic driver failure. Rust's sicp-machine escapes the same range via \uXXXX; latent because no corpus transcript emits control characters.

rawResults.suggestion: Resolve the oracle classpath from Gradle itself (a task printing the resolved runtime classpath for the compiler configuration) instead of duplicating version literals and list positions.
rawResults.description: The native oracle reconstructs the K2JVMCompiler classpath by hardcoding its dependency versions (kotlin-reflect 1.6.10, kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm 1.8.0, annotations 23.0.0 alongside the 2.4.20 artifacts) and selects the stdlib positionally via jars[2]; a Gradle resolution change (e.g. the embedded compiler bumping its own deps) makes findJar miss, collapsing every native comparison into a driver failure rather than a case defect.

rawResults.suggestion: Add the four section-8.2 witnesses as negative admission tests asserting Admission.admit rejects each (asserting the category, not the wording).
rawResults.description: The section 8.2 negative witnesses (bad-nonboolean-cond, bad-nullable-cond, bad-val-reassign, and one more) are explicitly documented 'gate rejection UNRUN', and no Kotlin test exercises them — GuestAdmissionTest covers only declaration-shape rejections — so the admission gate's core host-invalid rejections are unverified anywhere, unlike Rust whose borrow-error/raw-pointer witnesses are pinned by witness_classes.rs.

rawResults.suggestion: Set node-version to '24.21.0' (or invoke the conformance step through the same mise-pinned PATH the justfile uses).
rawResults.description: The TypeScript CI job selects node-version: '24' (floating latest 24.x) while the repository pins Node 24.21.0 via mise (typescript/justfile:4 and the root justfile's test-conformance PATH prepend), so CI gates and the conformance run execute on an unpinned runtime — contradicting the toolchain pin the current HEAD commit ('Pin the Node toolchain and correct the public claims') establishes.

rawResults.suggestion: Verify manifest_sha256 against the loaded cases bytes at harness startup (and baseline_commit against the git rev), or remove the fields.
rawResults.description: Top-level manifest_sha256 and baseline_commit are never verified by tools/host_conformance_check.py (its only sha256 use is per-case report metadata), so the recorded provenance claims are dead metadata that can drift silently from the cases on disk.

rawResults.suggestion: Use aa.checked_add(bb) == Some(cc) to mirror the teaching arm's checked arithmetic.
rawResults.description: reference_holds' Pythagorean arm computes 'aa + bb' with a raw + while the teaching try_holds uses checked_add; with operands above ~3e9 the debug build panics (release wraps), crashing the reference driver instead of failing the guard — a duplicated-but-divergent arithmetic path in an 'independent' oracle. Latent: corpus ranges cap at 12.

rawResults.suggestion: No change needed — see falsePositiveReason.
rawResults.description: Query/machine .mts artifacts bypass the admission checker entirely (dynamic import of the copied module via importCase); source.ts units go through admitSource but data modules do not.
rawResults.falsePositiveReason: Contract-intended: query/machine artifacts are native TypeScript data modules, not guest source; the harness still type-checks every .mts via native_compile (host_conformance_check.py:272-282), so nothing admits unchecked code.

rawResults.suggestion: No change needed — see falsePositiveReason.
rawResults.description: Kotlin machine cases use different inputs than other editions under the same case ids (01/04 use a=1071,b=462; OCaml/TypeScript/Rust use a=206,b=40; factorial n=5 vs 6; fibonacci n=7 vs 10/8/6).
rawResults.falsePositiveReason: Per-edition divergence is contract-permitted: the oracle is per-edition (engine vs reference/native within one edition), and nothing in the plan or cases.json pins shared inputs across editions.

rawResults.suggestion: No change needed — see falsePositiveReason.
rawResults.description: The OCaml reference models share Constructor_data (fixture literal parser), Env, Prelude, Ast and Value with the teaching engines rather than reimplementing them.
rawResults.falsePositiveReason: The independence boundary covers the engine under test (eval/apply, machine execution, qeval): each model implements its own evaluator/interpreter and shares only data-language vocabulary — the same accepted boundary as TypeScript's shared AST and Kotlin's shared Admission/GValue.

rawResults.suggestion: Desugar compound assignment at parse or apply `Primitives.binary(operator.dropLast(1), current, value)` in each engine's assign/write path, including member and index targets.
rawResults.description: `Assignment.operator` is never applied by any engine: Direct.assign, Analyzed.assignmentExec, SearchModule.writeAssignment, ch5 ExplicitControl.evalAssignment, and Compiler.compileAssignment all store `eval(statement.value)` directly, so an admitted `x += 2` (checker-validated by checkCompound) assigns 2 instead of x+2 — silent wrong-answer divergence from the host.

rawResults.suggestion: Reset `loopDepth` to 0 when entering a lambda body (save/restore around lambdaType and zeroArgLambdaType), mirroring the narrowings snapshot.
rawResults.description: `loopDepth` (incremented by checkWhile/checkFor) is not reset at a lambda boundary: lambdaType/zeroArgLambdaType create a `lambdaBoundary=true` scope but leave loopDepth intact, so `while (c) { val f = { break } }` is admitted though kotlinc rejects break/continue inside lambdas (grammar: break/continue apply only to an enclosing while/for).

rawResults.suggestion: Begin a loan on the receiver's root binding whenever a method returns a reference or iterator derived from it (Iter/IterMut/VecGet/MapGet/VecGetMut/MapGetMut/BoxAsRef/BoxAsMut), retargeted to the result holder by settle_initializer_loans; add Iter to needs_place.
rawResults.description: Borrows created by methods are never registered: `begin_loan` is called only for explicit `&place` borrows (line 1863) and closure captures, so `let it = v.iter(); v.push(1)`, `let r = v.get_mut(0); v.push(1)`, and `for x in v.iter() { v.push(x) }` are all admitted though rustc rejects them (the iterator/reference keeps a live borrow). `Iter` is even absent from `needs_place`, so `vec![1,2].iter().next()` admits a borrow of a dropped temporary.

rawResults.suggestion: Gate the mutating members (`add`, `set`, `put`, `remove`) on the Mutable* receiver names and return Outside for the read-only ones.
rawResults.description: collectionCall admits `add` and `set` on every List/Collection/Set/MutableList and mapCall admits `put`/`remove` on Map and MutableMap with no mutability check — `listOf(1).add(2)` or `mapOf("k" to 1).put("k", 2)` pass admission though kotlinc rejects them (immutable List/Set/Map have no such members); the runtime then dies with UnassignedRead. Host-invalid programs reach the guest.

rawResults.suggestion: Replace the member denylist with per-object allowlists (Math: the six admitted functions) and reject member access on process/globalThis outright.
rawResults.description: FORBIDDEN_MEMBERS is a denylist (Math.random, Date.now, performance.now) where the grammar §4.1 requires a closed allowlist (Math: abs/floor/max/min/sqrt/trunc only; time sources and host services excluded). `Math.log`, `Math.PI`, `Date.UTC`, `process.env`, `process.exit(1)`, and `globalThis.eval(...)` are all admitted — member calls on forbidden globals bypass FORBIDDEN_CALLEES entirely since it only matches a bare-identifier callee.

rawResults.suggestion: Reject Return nodes reached while checking a lambda body (track a lambda-boundary flag on the scope, like loopDepth should be), or reject Return in expression position inside lambdas.
rawResults.description: `return` inside a lambda is admitted: Return is both a Statement and an Expression (dispatchExpression ~905), and checkReturn uses `currentReturn` which lambdaType swaps to the lambda's result type — so `val f = { return 5 }` is admitted though kotlinc rejects returns in lambdas (no label). The engines then give it lambda-return semantics, compounding the divergence.

rawResults.suggestion: Apply the narrowing only when the Is node sits in a condition position (the narrowCondition path), not for every evaluated `is` expression.
rawResults.description: `isType` calls `narrow()` unconditionally on a non-negated `Is`, so the narrowing is observable inside one enclosing expression even without condition flow: `f(x is Foo, x.field)` admits a narrowed member read on x that Kotlin does not smart-cast (the `is` result is a Boolean value, not a guard).

rawResults.suggestion: Conform each value pattern's type to the subject type (conformOrFail(pattern, subjectType)).
rawResults.description: `checkValuePattern` checks the branch pattern with expected type null and never conforms it to the `when` subject type, so `when (x: Int) { "s" -> ...; else -> ... }` is admitted though kotlinc reports incompatible types.

rawResults.suggestion: Check the unwrapped receiver is non-nullable before indexing (reject Nullable receivers or require a safe call).
rawResults.description: `indexType` applies `coreType` (which unwraps Nullable) to the receiver, so `l[0]` on a `List<Int>?` is admitted though kotlinc requires `?.`; memberCall/memberValue on the same receiver do enforce `?.` — an inconsistent gap.

rawResults.suggestion: Require all alternatives to share one non-Free type (e.g. fail on the first sameType mismatch) and use it as the result; with T_FREE tolerated only as an unforced inference cell.
rawResults.description: `choose`/`chooseRandom` collapse mismatched alternative types to T_FREE via `reduceOrNull { a, b -> if (sameType(a,b)) a else T_FREE }`, after which the `alternatives share one type` check is vacuous (sameType(x, T_FREE) is always true) — `choose(1, "s")` is admitted as T_FREE, so `val x: Int = choose(1,"s")` types as Int while holding a String. The Bad branch is dead code.

rawResults.suggestion: In zeroArgBody, conform `body.result` to the expected `result` (sameType check) instead of answering the expected type unconditionally — or verify it in the ifFail arm.
rawResults.description: `ifFail` relies on `zeroArgBody(args, primary.type)` for the fallback, but zeroArgBody returns `Ok(result)` whenever a concrete expected type is passed — it never conforms the fallback body's actual result (`if (result == T_FREE) body.result else result`), so `ifFail({ 1 }, { "s" })` is admitted and typed Int though the fallback produces String.

rawResults.suggestion: Reject duplicate names when hoisting block-scope FunctionDecls and when local declarations collide with a hoisted name.
rawResults.description: Block-scope redeclarations are silently overwritten: declareLocalFunction (line 561) and checkLocalProperty (lines 609–617) write `scope.bindings[name] = ...` unconditionally with no duplicate check (rejectDuplicate covers only top-level collectHeaders and methodTable), so `val x = 1; val x = 2`, `fun f() {}; fun f() {}`, or `fun f() {}; val f = 1` in a block are admitted though kotlinc reports conflicting declarations.

rawResults.suggestion: Mark minus/take/drop/sorted results asSet = false (Kotlin returns List for all of them) and keep asSet only where the result is genuinely a Set.
rawResults.description: Set-ness leaks through collection ops: Primitives.collectionMember `minus` always returns `asSet = true` even for a List receiver (Kotlin `List - e` is a List), and `take`/`drop`/`sorted` propagate the receiver's asSet flag to results the checker types as List — so `setOf(1,2).take(1) + 1` yields [1] under the engine but [1,1] natively.

rawResults.suggestion: Require sameType(step.result, arguments[0]) before answering Ok(arguments[0]).
rawResults.description: `fold` verifies the step's two parameters against (initial, element) but never checks the step's result conforms to the accumulator type — `xs.fold(0) { a: Int, x: Int -> true }` is admitted and typed Int though the lambda returns Boolean (kotlinc rejects).

rawResults.suggestion: Report FORBIDDEN_CALLEES also on a `variable` expression whose name is in the table (so the binding is refused at the read site).
rawResults.description: The forbidden-callee check fires only when the callee is a bare identifier: `const e = eval; e("x")` binds eval to a new name and the later call through `e` is admitted (variable reads are checked only against the pending set), bypassing the eval ban the FORBIDDEN_CALLEES table states.

rawResults.suggestion: Require the suffixed type to equal the scrutinee's type: `(Some(I64), HostTy::I64)` and `(Some(Usize), HostTy::Usize)` only.
rawResults.description: Integer-literal patterns with an explicit suffix ignore the scrutinee type: `(Some(I64), _)` and `(Some(Usize), _)` accept regardless of the matched type, so `match u: usize { 5i64 => ... }` or `match s: String { 5i64 => ... }` is admitted though rustc reports mismatched types.

rawResults.suggestion: Add Next to the needs_mut and needs_place sets in enforce_receiver_mutability.
rawResults.description: `MethodOp::Next` is missing from `needs_mut` (and `needs_place`): `let it = v.iter(); it.next()` is admitted though `Iterator::next` takes `&mut self` and rustc requires `let mut it`.

rawResults.suggestion: Treat `HostTy::Box(inner)` as dereferenceable (referent = inner), or surface a BoxDeref projection in check_unary/place_of.
rawResults.description: `referent()` returns a referent only for `HostTy::Ref`, so `*b`, `(*b).f`, and `*b = v` on `Box<T>` are rejected by check_unary/place_of ("dereference needs a reference") though Rust admits box dereference and move-out — an under-admission of host-valid programs.

rawResults.suggestion: Verify abrupt completion for the final non-empty clause (and each non-final one, rather than relying solely on noFallthrough).
rawResults.description: The grammar (§1.1) requires every non-empty switch case body to complete abruptly, but the switch arm only recurses into a shared scope — the final clause is never checked, so `switch (x) { case 1: f(); }` is admitted though the contract says such a body is rejected (tsc's noFallthroughCasesInSwitch does not cover the last clause).

rawResults.suggestion: Include TypeKind::Zip in the receiver sets for "next" and "enumerate" (and "zip" if zipped iterators may chain further).
rawResults.description: `TypeKind::Zip` is absent from the `next`/`enumerate` receiver kinds, so `zip.next()` and `it.zip(w).enumerate()` are rejected as outside the allowlist though the grammar admits iterator chains "possibly chained through next, enumerate, zip" — host-valid programs are under-admitted.

rawResults.suggestion: Loop the ref peel (or recurse) in check_pattern until a non-Ref scrutinee remains, matching the runtime's match_through_ref.
rawResults.description: check_pattern peels only one `Ref` layer, so `match &&opt { Some(..) => }` is rejected while rustc's match ergonomics read through every layer (the ops-side match_through_ref already handles multi-level reads) — under-admission of host-valid code.

rawResults.suggestion: Emit Diag::unsupported for &str ordering (host-valid but outside the subset) rather than a type error.
rawResults.description: `&str` ordering (`a < b` on string slices) is rejected via `Diag::type_error` — the grammar's rejection taxonomy requires `Diag::unsupported` for host-valid-but-excluded constructs (§6), so the diagnostic class is mislabeled for a host-valid program.

rawResults.suggestion: Apply the same field-level `implements(Hash)` check for the Hash derive as Eq/PartialEq.
rawResults.description: check_item_derives verifies fields implement PartialEq only for Eq — `#[derive(Hash)]` on a type with a non-Hash field (e.g. a HashMap field) is admitted though rustc rejects the derived impl.

rawResults.suggestion: Treat a Unit arm like any other arm in unifyBranches (or flag an Int/String arm mixing with Unit as a Bad surface result).
rawResults.description: `whenType` skips unification when the running `result` is T_UNIT (`if (result == T_UNIT) branchType else unifyBranches`), so `when (x) { A -> Unit; B -> "s" }` types as String — kotlinc would join the arms to a common supertype (Any-ish) and a Unit arm is not special.

rawResults.suggestion: Walk StringTemplate fragments, Index/Member receivers, and any other expression nodes that can contain calls.
rawResults.description: walkTailExpression's `else -> {}` arm misses self-calls inside StringTemplate fragments, Index, and Member receivers, so `tailrec fun f(n) = "${f(n-1)}"` (a recursive call in a non-tail interpolation) is admitted though Kotlin's tailrec requires the self-call to be in tail position.

rawResults.suggestion: Remove the field or assert it equals the computed frame_slots (cheap consistency check).
rawResults.description: `FnCtx.slots` is incremented at line 256 but never read — `frame_slots` is computed independently as `next_bind - bind_base`; the field is dead state carried through every function check.

rawResults.suggestion: Either reject relative imports as UnsupportedSyntax in the subset checker, or stage the referenced edition-local units beside guest.ts.
rawResults.description: The admission workspace writes only `guest.ts` under `include: ["*.ts"]`, so a guest `import { x } from "./other.ts"` — which the grammar permits for "edition-local typed modules" — always fails with a host TS2307 module-not-found; the imports clause is unexercisable through admitSource.

rawResults.suggestion: Track readonly-ness through member chains (or rely on tsc and drop the partial local check).
rawResults.description: `checkMemberWrite` looks up readonly fields only when the receiver is an annotated variable — `a.b.f = 1` (where `b`'s field is readonly) and any write on an unannotated receiver skip the check — though the pinned tsc still rejects, so the gap is diagnostic coverage, not admission.
rawResults.falsePositiveReason: The pinned tsc layer still rejects readonly writes, so no host-invalid program is admitted; the local check is belt-and-suspenders whose narrower coverage only changes which diagnostic layer reports the error.

rawResults.suggestion: Emit the header once at the top of the file like the kotlin/typescript/ocaml manifests.
rawResults.description: The 4-line column-header comment block is repeated before every one of the 39 case rows (~273 comment lines where the other editions' manifests use 2–7 lines) — generated duplication that obscures the actual manifest rows.

rawResults.suggestion: Pin the runtime to the committed contract: `node-version-file: typescript/.node-version` (or `node-version: "24.21.0"`).
rawResults.description: `node-version: "24"` floats to the latest 24.x while typescript/package.json pins engines.node to exactly "24.21.0" and typescript/.npmrc sets engine-strict=true, so `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fails with ERR_PNPM_UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE on any 24.x release newer or older than 24.21.0 — the typescript job is broken-by-drift (or already red).

rawResults.suggestion: Track failures in the loop (e.g. `failed=0; ... || failed=1; done; exit $failed`) so any edition's nonzero scaffold result surfaces.
rawResults.description: The `scaffold` recipe's edition loop has no `set -e` and no failure accumulator, so the recipe's exit status is only the LAST edition's (kotlin) result — an unsolved scaffold in rust, ocaml, or typescript is silently reported as solved, defeating the recipe's documented 'nonzero while one is unsolved' contract.

rawResults.suggestion: Add `--locked` to the opam install line so CI consumes the committed lock.
rawResults.description: The ocaml job installs with `opam install . --deps-only --with-test --with-dev-setup` and omits `--locked`, so the committed ocaml/modern-sicp.opam.locked is ignored and dependency versions re-resolve from opam-repository on every run — floating versions against the repo's pinned contract (the ocaml/justfile setup recipe passes --locked).

rawResults.suggestion: Run the gates with `uv run --locked --project tools` (or add `uv lock --check`) so lock drift fails loudly.
rawResults.description: Every `uv run --project tools ...` invocation (and the justfile recipes it mirrors) runs without `--locked`/`--frozen`, so a stale or edited tools/uv.lock is silently re-locked to the newest compatible versions instead of failing — an unpinned-deps path inside otherwise frozen installs.

rawResults.suggestion: Pin uv: `with: version: "<exact>"`.
rawResults.description: All seven `astral-sh/setup-uv` uses omit `version:`, so the uv binary itself installs 'latest' on every run — a floating tool version that can change gate behavior or break all jobs at once, unlike every other action/tool in this workflow which is pinned.

rawResults.suggestion: Drop the `|| true` (or guard with an explicit `[ -f ... ]` test like the figures directory above it).
rawResults.description: Site assembly copies `$lang-sicp.pdf` with `|| true` while the sibling epub `cp` fails loudly — a missing or failed PDF artifact is silently swallowed and the Pages deploy ships an edition without its PDF.

rawResults.suggestion: Fail fast when the pinned node is absent, or assert `node --version` == 24.21.0 before running the checker.
rawResults.description: `test-conformance` prepends the hardcoded mise path `~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.21.0/bin` for the bare-`node` TypeScript driver, but on hosts without that mise install (nvm/system node) the recipe silently falls through to whatever node is on PATH — the pinned-runtime contract the comment promises is unverified.

rawResults.suggestion: Align CI commands with the declared canonical commands (`--locked` flags, `dune build`), or update the table so `just` and CI cannot diverge.
rawResults.description: CI gate commands drift from the canonical gate table (docs/plan/technical-modern-sicp-editions.md): rust clippy/nextest/test drop `--locked` (the same file's conformance driver.json uses it), and the ocaml step runs `dune build @check` instead of the declared `dune build`, so link-level failures the canonical gate would catch are invisible to CI. The adjacent `dune fmt --check 2>/dev/null || dune build @fmt` also hides a genuine fmt crash behind stderr suppression.

rawResults.suggestion: If the contract is 'report only', fine; otherwise return 1 when targets/unresolvable/deferred are nonzero.
rawResults.description: main() returns 0 unconditionally: `--check` mode reports overflowing/unresolvable figures but always exits 0, and `--apply` exits 0 even when edits are deferred or a scope violation is reported — would silently pass if ever wired as a gate.
rawResults.falsePositiveReason: It is a manual maintenance sweep, not a gate: nothing in justfile/CI invokes it, and its docstring defines --check as report-only, so exit 0 is intended behavior today.

rawResults.suggestion: No change needed where rustup provides shims (CI/dev docs assume rustup); document the assumption or invoke `rustup run 1.98.1 rustc` for robustness.
rawResults.description: `native_compile` invokes `rustc +1.98.1`, which requires rustc on PATH to be a rustup shim — on a host where rustc is a direct binary (system package, no rustup) the flag is treated as a filename and the check errors.
rawResults.falsePositiveReason: rustc +toolchain is valid rustup-proxy syntax, and both CI and the documented setup install via rustup, so the shim is always in place.

rawResults.suggestion: Analyze each branch's pattern once at procedure-analysis time and reuse the result.
rawResults.description: branchMatches re-analyzes each when/match branch's pattern every time control reaches the branch, so a match with k branches does O(k) analysis work per evaluation.

rawResults.suggestion: Cache the analyzed body on the method value and execute it directly per call.
rawResults.description: methodValue re-runs analyzeBody on the method body at every call instead of reusing the analyzed closure, so all method invocation path pays the full analysis cost per call.

rawResults.suggestion: Index frames by position or precompute a name->slot map so reads are O(1).
rawResults.description: Compiled variable reads resolve lexical addresses with elementAtOrNull over a LinkedHashMap, a linear scan per variable access in compiled code.

rawResults.suggestion: Record only mutated cells (write-log / trail) and restore those instead of whole-env snapshots.
rawResults.description: snapshotCells/restoreCells copy every environment cell at each choose point and each retry, making each choice step O(total cells).

rawResults.suggestion: Thread a persistent deque/iterator through the CPS chain instead of copying lists per step.
rawResults.description: Callback chains build accumulated continuations with drop(1) + appended state per step, giving O(n^2) work over n nested callbacks.

rawResults.suggestion: Pool or intern function wrappers and bound the closures table to live choice points.
rawResults.description: Per-call VFunction allocations plus an unbounded closures map grow memory with call count during search.

rawResults.suggestion: Trampoline the continuation chain or use a heap-allocated frame to make iteration constant-stack.
rawResults.description: The amb evaluator's CPS nests one JVM frame per loop iteration/step with no trampolining, so deep iteration exhausts the stack where the oracle is iterative.

rawResults.suggestion: Back the guest map with a mutable LinkedHashMap and do in-place put/remove.
rawResults.description: Map mutation builtins do linear scans, rebuild mapOf per write, and entries.removeIf per update, making n map updates O(n^2).

rawResults.suggestion: Cache the realized length on the lazy-list node or bound materialization.
