items.suggestion: Pool or intern function wrappers and bound the closures table to live choice points.

items.description: snapshotCells/restoreCells copy every environment cell at each choose point and each retry, making each choice step O(total cells).
items.suggestion: Record only mutated cells (write-log / trail) and restore those instead of whole-env snapshots.

items.description: Callback chains build accumulated continuations with drop(1) + appended state per step, giving O(n^2) work over n nested callbacks.
items.suggestion: Thread a persistent deque/iterator through the CPS chain instead of copying lists per step.

items.description: sicp_range materializes the entire range eagerly instead of yielding lazily.
items.suggestion: Represent ranges as a (start,end,step) descriptor iterated on demand.

items.description: Compiled variable reads resolve lexical addresses with elementAtOrNull over a LinkedHashMap, a linear scan per variable access in compiled code.
items.suggestion: Index frames by position or precompute a name->slot map so reads are O(1).

items.description: The teaching machine path silently defaults where grammar.md:477-478 pins 'Registers start unassigned; a read before any write raises UnassignedRegister': MachineScript.parse seeds every registers-line name to 0L (237-238) and machineEngine writes VLong(0) into each (168-170), so declared-but-unwritten registers read 0; const for an undeclared register is silently dropped (?: continue, 169); every op defaults missing args to VLong(0L) and asLong maps non-numeric operands to 0L (263-298) instead of ShapeFault — and 'rem' with one operand computes '% 0' as a raw ArithmeticException, violating 'engine implementations report the category, never raw host exceptions' (grammar:373); renderRegister renders non-numeric register content as "0" (186-194).
items.suggestion: Seed only const lines (leave declared registers VUnassigned), raise UnassignedRegister/ShapeFault on missing or mis-shaped operands, and render unassigned registers as a marker rather than 0.

items.description: MachineScript.parse indexes and converts unchecked: parts[1].toLong() (line 242) on `const` lines, words[1] in test/branch/goto/save/restore/perform (lines 302-314), source[1].toLong() for `const` sources (line 320), and operand.drop(1).toLong() for `#` operands (line 326) — a malformed .machine case (missing operand, non-numeric literal, empty source list) throws NumberFormatException/IndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning null for a `rejected` observation.
items.suggestion: Guard arity before indexing and use toLongOrNull (or catch NumberFormatException) inside MachineScript.parse so malformed input yields null → rejected.

items.description: accumulateArg/advanceSeq/whileStartBody copy whole frames and drop(1) operand lists per step, giving O(k^2)/O(s^2) per call and sequence.
items.suggestion: Keep a mutable arg accumulator and advance sequences by index rather than copying lists.

items.description: Query fixture decoding uses unchecked casts and lookups on guest-produced values: `items(variables).map { hostTerm(it) as QVar }`, `(value as GValue.VObject).className`, `.fields.getValue(name)`, `(value as GValue.VList).items`, plus the 4-element destructure `val (facts, rules, query, variables) = values` — an admitted guest program returning a wrongly-shaped values list throws ClassCastException/NoSuchElementException/IndexOutOfBoundsException instead of an error/rejected observation.
items.suggestion: Validate the values list shape and each node's GValue tag before casting; emit a DriverFailure-style rejected/error observation on mismatch.

items.description: The reference machine-script model repeats the same unchecked parsing: registers[parts[0]] = parts[1].toLong() (line 1089), words[1] label/register indexing (lines 1129-1179), and source[0]/source[1] access with toLong (lines 1189-1201) — malformed .machine input crashes the reference engine with a JVM exception rather than producing an error/rejected observation.
items.suggestion: Apply the same arity/numeric guards as suggested for Driver.kt's MachineScript (or share a single validated parser between teaching and reference paths).

items.description: MachineModel — the reference oracle for machine cases — silently defaults on every malformed-input class the grammar pins as typed errors (grammar.md:370-371 UnassignedRegister/ShapeFault): unknown instruction -> pc+1 (1143), goto/branch unknown label -> pc+1 (1129-1132), save/operand/sourceValue on an unassigned register -> 0L (1135/1190/1202), restore underflow -> 0L (1139), unknown test op -> false (1169), unknown perform op -> skipped (1181), unknown compute op -> left (1215). The teaching Machine raises UnassignedRegister/ShapeFault on the same conditions (Machine.kt:249/333/400/405/430), so the oracle fabricates deterministic-but-wrong observations instead of checking the error contract — duplicated-but-divergent machine semantics, invisible on the well-formed corpus.
items.suggestion: Make MachineModel raise the same typed categories as Machine for unknown labels/instructions/ops, unassigned reads, and stack underflow (or share MachineScript's strict decode instead of re-lexing lines).

items.description: Block-scope redeclarations are silently overwritten: declareLocalFunction (line 561) and checkLocalProperty (lines 609–617) write `scope.bindings[name] = ...` unconditionally with no duplicate check (rejectDuplicate covers only top-level collectHeaders and methodTable), so `val x = 1; val x = 2`, `fun f() {}; fun f() {}`, or `fun f() {}; val f = 1` in a block are admitted though kotlinc reports conflicting declarations.
items.suggestion: Reject duplicate names when hoisting block-scope FunctionDecls and when local declarations collide with a hoisted name.

items.description: `return` inside a lambda is admitted: Return is both a Statement and an Expression (dispatchExpression ~905), and checkReturn uses `currentReturn` which lambdaType swaps to the lambda's result type — so `val f = { return 5 }` is admitted though kotlinc rejects returns in lambdas (no label). The engines then give it lambda-return semantics, compounding the divergence.
items.suggestion: Reject Return nodes reached while checking a lambda body (track a lambda-boundary flag on the scope, like loopDepth should be), or reject Return in expression position inside lambdas.

items.description: ~30 rejection categories are implemented but tests assert roughly 8 (UndeclaredName, Redeclaration, MiscKotlin, TypeMismatch, UserGenerics, TypeInference, WrongArgumentType, ExpectedNumber-adjacent); MixedWidthArithmetic, LiteralRange, NonExhaustiveWhen, SealedWhenElse, PropertySmartCast, RecursiveValLambda, Reflection, StructuredOutput, Sequence, CharSurface, ImplicitIt, WrongArity, ValReassignment, NamedDefaultVarargs, DuplicateArgument, NonBooleanCondition, NullableCondition, MixedEquality, ImplicitWidthChange and the tailrec-position check are never exercised.
items.suggestion: Table-test one minimal rejecting source per category string in GuestAdmissionTest so every failUnsupported site is pinned.

items.description: `isType` calls `narrow()` unconditionally on a non-negated `Is`, so the narrowing is observable inside one enclosing expression even without condition flow: `f(x is Foo, x.field)` admits a narrowed member read on x that Kotlin does not smart-cast (the `is` result is a Boolean value, not a guard).
items.suggestion: Apply the narrowing only when the Is node sits in a condition position (the narrowCondition path), not for every evaluated `is` expression.
items.fpReason: checkExpression (Checker.kt:838-848) saves/restores narrowings around every expression, so narrow() evaluated as a value is dead state — `x is A; println(x.n)` already rejects (probed).

items.description: `checkValuePattern` checks the branch pattern with expected type null and never conforms it to the `when` subject type, so `when (x: Int) { "s" -> ...; else -> ... }` is admitted though kotlinc reports incompatible types.
items.suggestion: Conform each value pattern's type to the subject type (conformOrFail(pattern, subjectType)).

items.description: `indexType` applies `coreType` (which unwraps Nullable) to the receiver, so `l[0]` on a `List<Int>?` is admitted though kotlinc requires `?.`; memberCall/memberValue on the same receiver do enforce `?.` — an inconsistent gap.
items.suggestion: Check the unwrapped receiver is non-nullable before indexing (reject Nullable receivers or require a safe call).

items.description: lambdaHeadFollows probes by re-parsing ahead of the cursor at each `{`, so nested blocks re-scan suffixes repeatedly (~O(2^depth) on deep nesting).
items.suggestion: Disambiguate with a bounded token lookahead instead of a speculative full re-parse.

items.description: `size` on VLazyList materializes the whole spine to count it; the lazy corpus calls xs.size inside a while loop, so each loop pays full traversal.
items.suggestion: Cache the realized length on the lazy-list node or bound materialization.

items.description: Map mutation builtins do linear scans, rebuild mapOf per write, and entries.removeIf per update, making n map updates O(n^2).
items.suggestion: Back the guest map with a mutable LinkedHashMap and do in-place put/remove.

items.description: lazyListMember materializes the spine before scanning membership, forcing the whole lazy structure for a membership probe.
items.suggestion: Scan the lazy spine incrementally and short-circuit on the first match.

items.description: Set-ness leaks through collection ops: Primitives.collectionMember `minus` always returns `asSet = true` even for a List receiver (Kotlin `List - e` is a List), and `take`/`drop`/`sorted` propagate the receiver's asSet flag to results the checker types as List — so `setOf(1,2).take(1) + 1` yields [1] under the engine but [1,1] natively.
items.suggestion: Mark minus/take/drop/sorted results asSet = false (Kotlin returns List for all of them) and keep asSet only where the result is genuinely a Set.

items.description: `choose`/`chooseRandom` collapse mismatched alternative types to T_FREE via `reduceOrNull { a, b -> if (sameType(a,b)) a else T_FREE }`, after which the `alternatives share one type` check is vacuous (sameType(x, T_FREE) is always true) — `choose(1, "s")` is admitted as T_FREE, so `val x: Int = choose(1,"s")` types as Int while holding a String. The Bad branch is dead code.
items.suggestion: Require all alternatives to share one non-Free type (e.g. fail on the first sameType mismatch) and use it as the result; with T_FREE tolerated only as an unforced inference cell.

items.description: `ifFail` relies on `zeroArgBody(args, primary.type)` for the fallback, but zeroArgBody returns `Ok(result)` whenever a concrete expected type is passed — it never conforms the fallback body's actual result (`if (result == T_FREE) body.result else result`), so `ifFail({ 1 }, { "s" })` is admitted and typed Int though the fallback produces String.
items.suggestion: In zeroArgBody, conform `body.result` to the expected `result` (sameType check) instead of answering the expected type unconditionally — or verify it in the ifFail arm.

items.description: `fold` verifies the step's two parameters against (initial, element) but never checks the step's result conforms to the accumulator type — `xs.fold(0) { a: Int, x: Int -> true }` is admitted and typed Int though the lambda returns Boolean (kotlinc rejects).
items.suggestion: Require sameType(step.result, arguments[0]) before answering Ok(arguments[0]).

items.description: 1,273-LOC four-stage admission checker (closed-grammar parse, unsupported-forms walk, pinned typechecker with warning-8 capture, contract walk) is tested by 59-LOC test_check.ml (~12 cases exercising each kind once); contract edges — nested/or-pattern non-exhaustiveness, equality on functions/tuples/records, prelude boundary entries, line-directive remapping, and warning-8 classification — are untested.
items.suggestion: Expand test_check.ml into per-stage case matrices, especially contract-walk boundary programs (admitted vs rejected near-miss pairs).

items.description: lower_scalar calls `int_of_string s` whenever valid_int_literal passes, but valid_int_literal only checks the character alphabet — an all-digit literal exceeding max_int (e.g. 99999999999999999999, which the OCaml parser stores as a raw string) makes int_of_string raise Failure, an uncaught exception that crashes Check.check instead of producing a `rejected` diagnostic.
items.suggestion: Wrap the conversion (int_of_string_opt) and emit syntax_at at "integer literal out of range" on overflow.

items.description: table_find/table_replace do linear searches and rebuild via rest @ [key,value] per Hashtbl op, making n ops O(n^2).
items.suggestion: Use a real Hashtbl or mutable bucket list for the guest table.

items.description: env_find does List.assoc_opt over a flat association list, so variable lookup is O(total bindings) per access.
items.suggestion: Keep per-frame hash tables or index bindings by slot.

items.description: Machine_model resolves label targets by a linear instruction scan on every goto/branch, so loops pay O(program length) per jump.
items.suggestion: Precompute a label->instruction-index map at assembly.

items.description: env.clone() on every Let/thunk creation and captured.clone() per apply copies the whole environment per lazy step.
items.suggestion: Use Rc/persistent env sharing so captures extend rather than copy.

items.description: reference_explore's ChooseRange/ChooseFrom loops call reference_rollback(trail, bindings, trail.len() - 1) after each body exploration, popping exactly the last trail entry instead of everything pushed since the variable's bind (the teaching engine's rollback_binding(var) at line 322 pops all entries since and including var's bind). Trailed Set writes inside a loop body therefore leak into later iterations of the reference model — a rollback-discipline divergence in the very property the amb/03 lesson note ('trailed assignment rollback') claims to check. Latent because no corpus Search program places a Set inside a ChooseRange/ChooseFrom body.
items.suggestion: Capture mark = trail.len() before reference_bind (or pop until var's own trail entry inclusive) so the reference mirrors rollback_binding.

items.description: Rust experiment-case JSON descriptors carry only a constructor name, so fixture correctness exists only inside the binary: search_prime_sum encodes Or(SumEq(i+j,7), SumEq(i+j,11)) with a literal pair of 'taught primes' instead of the real primality predicate that Kotlin (isPrime over 1..4), OCaml (prime/prime_test), and TypeScript (isPrime over chosen lists) implement for the same amb/02-prime-sum-pair case. Engine and oracle share the constructor table, so a weaker or wrong program is conformance-invisible.
items.suggestion: Give each case descriptor a minimal checkable expectation (answer count, or an expected-stdout hash) reviewed against the canonical case intent, or embed the real predicate program rather than its hand-picked answers.

items.description: unify's walk clones both whole terms per unify step, duplicating term structure on each extension.
items.suggestion: Unify by reference with a union/bind table rather than cloning terms.

items.description: machine/01-gcd and machine/04-gcd-print both resolve to the same gcd_machine constructor with the same inputs (206/40), so the two case identities run literally the same program — the per-step perform-print lesson that OCaml (prints every remainder t) and Kotlin (prints every a) implement under 04-gcd-print collapses into a duplicate of 01 in the Rust suite. machine_reference hand-derives only the final answer, so nothing flags that the distinct lesson is uncovered.
items.suggestion: Give machine/04 its own monitored-print controller (or a distinct constructor + reference transcript emitting each remainder) so the case identity exercises the effect lesson.

items.description: GC relocate looks up relocated addresses with a linear .find over moved cells, making collection O(n^2) in live pairs.
items.suggestion: Store the forwarding address on the cell (or a HashMap) like a Cheney collector.

items.description: Loop execution re-arms by cloning body/test/pat AST per iteration.
items.suggestion: Hold loop AST by reference/Arc across iterations.

items.description: `MethodOp::Next` is missing from `needs_mut` (and `needs_place`): `let it = v.iter(); it.next()` is admitted though `Iterator::next` takes `&mut self` and rustc requires `let mut it`.
items.suggestion: Add Next to the needs_mut and needs_place sets in enforce_receiver_mutability.

items.description: Integer-literal patterns with an explicit suffix ignore the scrutinee type: `(Some(I64), _)` and `(Some(Usize), _)` accept regardless of the matched type, so `match u: usize { 5i64 => ... }` or `match s: String { 5i64 => ... }` is admitted though rustc reports mismatched types.
items.suggestion: Require the suffixed type to equal the scrutinee's type: `(Some(I64), HostTy::I64)` and `(Some(Usize), HostTy::Usize)` only.

items.description: `referent()` returns a referent only for `HostTy::Ref`, so `*b`, `(*b).f`, and `*b = v` on `Box<T>` are rejected by check_unary/place_of ("dereference needs a reference") though Rust admits box dereference and move-out — an under-admission of host-valid programs.
items.suggestion: Treat `HostTy::Box(inner)` as dereferenceable (referent = inner), or surface a BoxDeref projection in check_unary/place_of.

items.description: write_at clones the whole container root for every projected write.
items.suggestion: Mutate through a shared interior cell (Rc<RefCell>) instead of cloning the root.

items.description: VecPush/MapInsert/MapRemove/StrPushStr clone the receiver on each mutation, so building a collection of n items is O(n^2).
items.suggestion: Mutate in place behind Rc<RefCell> or pre-reserve and update the container directly.

items.description: extend clones the entire Substitution map for each new binding, so a unify making k bindings is O(k^2).
items.suggestion: Use a persistent map or a mutable frame with an undo trail.

items.description: Case vocabulary admits only "value"/"error" observations (tools/host_conformance_check.py:129 rejects anything else) while the observation protocol accepts "rejected"; no conformance case can therefore pin an admission rejection, so the "rejected" emission path in every edition driver (rust sicp-eval emit, kotlin Driver.rejection, ts outcome.tag="rejected") is never exercised end-to-end.
items.suggestion: Either add a "rejected" observation kind to the inventory with per-edition out-of-subset corpus rows, or document that admission rejection is covered only by unit tests and fill the per-edition gaps.

items.description: The check_references rendered-book regression (3-case parametrization) and the relative-converter test pytest.skip when texi2any is absent — never installed in the CI tools job — so the rendered-source verification half of the book-structure gate is never exercised in CI.
items.suggestion: Run the texi2any-dependent tests under the books jobs' toolchain or install the pinned texi2any in the tools job.

items.description: Module-level `pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("makeinfo") is None)` skips the entire suite when makeinfo is missing, and the CI tools job (`uv run --project tools pytest tools/tests -q`) never installs texinfo — so the gate's log-parsing, listing-environment mapping and width-tolerance logic executes in no CI job.
items.suggestion: Install the pinned texinfo toolchain in the tools job (or run these tests inside the books jobs' environment) so the skip is never taken in CI.

items.description: Amb while/for-of loops recurse the JS stack once per iteration through nested synchronous CPS continuations, so deep iteration overflows where the oracle is iterative.
items.suggestion: Drive iterations through the deferred trampoline instead of nesting synchronous continuations.

items.description: Frame.extend rebuilds the array via [binding, ...frame] per binding and bindingInFrame linear-scans per lookup, so unifying k variables is O(k^2) copy + O(k) lookup.
items.suggestion: Use a persistent map or cons-list frames with a map for lookup.

items.description: The forbidden-callee check fires only when the callee is a bare identifier: `const e = eval; e("x")` binds eval to a new name and the later call through `e` is admitted (variable reads are checked only against the pending set), bypassing the eval ban the FORBIDDEN_CALLEES table states.
items.suggestion: Report FORBIDDEN_CALLEES also on a `variable` expression whose name is in the table (so the binding is refused at the read site).
items.fixedBy: e28a0b0 (resolve/pr9-codex-ts): variable case rejects unshadowed forbidden-global reads

items.description: adjoinArg copies the operand list per argument and ev-sequence/restOperands slices(1) per step, giving O(k^2) operand accumulation and O(s^2) sequence traversal.
items.suggestion: Accumulate operands in a mutable array and index sequences rather than slicing.

items.description: The 1,112-LOC conformance driver embeds all four reference models (AST-directed lazy/amb desugarer, query model, machine model, boundary narrowing helpers like toMachineProgram/fieldsOf) with no unit tests; a reference-side defect surfaces only as engine divergence, and a same-direction defect is masked entirely.
items.suggestion: Add unit tests for desugar/outermostExtensions/rewriteExtension, the narrowing helpers, and each reference model against hand-computed cases independent of the teaching engines.

items.description: All seven `astral-sh/setup-uv` uses omit `version:`, so the uv binary itself installs 'latest' on every run — a floating tool version that can change gate behavior or break all jobs at once, unlike every other action/tool in this workflow which is pinned.
items.suggestion: Pin uv: `with: version: "<exact>"`.

items.description: CI gate commands drift from the canonical gate table (docs/plan/technical-modern-sicp-editions.md): rust clippy/nextest/test drop `--locked` (the same file's conformance driver.json uses it), and the ocaml step runs `dune build @check` instead of the declared `dune build`, so link-level failures the canonical gate would catch are invisible to CI. The adjacent `dune fmt --check 2>/dev/null || dune build @fmt` also hides a genuine fmt crash behind stderr suppression.
items.suggestion: Align CI commands with the declared canonical commands (`--locked` flags, `dune build`), or update the table so `just` and CI cannot diverge.

items.description: The TypeScript CI job selects node-version: '24' (floating latest 24.x) while the repository pins Node 24.21.0 via mise (typescript/justfile:4 and the root justfile's test-conformance PATH prepend), so CI gates and the conformance run execute on an unpinned runtime — contradicting the toolchain pin the current HEAD commit ('Pin the Node toolchain and correct the public claims') establishes.
items.suggestion: Set node-version to '24.21.0' (or invoke the conformance step through the same mise-pinned PATH the justfile uses).
items.resolution: node-version pinned 24.21.0 in the same fix as the high at :72

items.description: Every `uv run --project tools ...` invocation (and the justfile recipes it mirrors) runs without `--locked`/`--frozen`, so a stale or edited tools/uv.lock is silently re-locked to the newest compatible versions instead of failing — an unpinned-deps path inside otherwise frozen installs.
items.suggestion: Run the gates with `uv run --locked --project tools` (or add `uv lock --check`) so lock drift fails loudly.

items.description: Site assembly copies `$lang-sicp.pdf` with `|| true` while the sibling epub `cp` fails loudly — a missing or failed PDF artifact is silently swallowed and the Pages deploy ships an edition without its PDF.
items.suggestion: Drop the `|| true` (or guard with an explicit `[ -f ... ]` test like the figures directory above it).

items.description: `test-conformance` prepends the hardcoded mise path `~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.21.0/bin` for the bare-`node` TypeScript driver, but on hosts without that mise install (nvm/system node) the recipe silently falls through to whatever node is on PATH — the pinned-runtime contract the comment promises is unverified.
items.suggestion: Fail fast when the pinned node is absent, or assert `node --version` == 24.21.0 before running the checker.

items.description: Each force calls sink.contents() twice, re-materializing the delayed stream contents per force.
items.suggestion: Materialize once and reuse the forced value.

items.description: Emitted C code resolves variables by walking a strcmp chain over the env list, so every variable access is O(env depth) string comparisons.
items.suggestion: Emit indexed slots or a small per-frame table instead of strcmp walking.

items.description: Emitted method dispatch walks the method list linearly per call.
items.suggestion: Emit a dispatch table indexed by method id.

items.description: Driver.escape omits control characters below 0x20 other than \n \r \t, so a transcript containing e.g. \u000b or NUL produces invalid JSON and the harness's one-object parse fails as a generic driver failure. Rust's sicp-machine escapes the same range via \uXXXX; latent because no corpus transcript emits control characters.
items.suggestion: Escape every ch < 0x20 as \u%04x (matching the Rust driver) so the emitted observation stays valid JSON for arbitrary transcripts.

items.description: The native oracle reconstructs the K2JVMCompiler classpath by hardcoding its dependency versions (kotlin-reflect 1.6.10, kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm 1.8.0, annotations 23.0.0 alongside the 2.4.20 artifacts) and selects the stdlib positionally via jars[2]; a Gradle resolution change (e.g. the embedded compiler bumping its own deps) makes findJar miss, collapsing every native comparison into a driver failure rather than a case defect.
items.suggestion: Resolve the oracle classpath from Gradle itself (a task printing the resolved runtime classpath for the compiler configuration) instead of duplicating version literals and list positions.

items.description: MachineModel privately re-implements the .machine line-protocol parser (a second parser beside Driver.MachineScript) and caps execution at a 1,000,000-step guard while the teaching Machine.run() has no bound; both paths are exercised only by the 4 corpus .machine files, so parser divergence on unexercised line forms or a non-terminating program is unguarded.
items.suggestion: Share one line-protocol parser between driver and reference model (or add parser-equivalence tests), and align the termination policy between teaching and reference machines.

items.description: modeOf/compose over LAZY/SEARCH/QUERY/QUERY_LAZY/QUERY_SEARCH and the UnsupportedComposition rejection have no unit tests — every admission test uses Mode.CORE except one Mode.QUERY call; the non-CORE modes are reachable only through positively-admitted corpus programs.
items.suggestion: Table-test module-set composition, including the LAZY+SEARCH combination that must reject with UnsupportedComposition.

items.description: walkTailExpression's `else -> {}` arm misses self-calls inside StringTemplate fragments, Index, and Member receivers, so `tailrec fun f(n) = "${f(n-1)}"` (a recursive call in a non-tail interpolation) is admitted though Kotlin's tailrec requires the self-call to be in tail position.
items.suggestion: Walk StringTemplate fragments, Index/Member receivers, and any other expression nodes that can contain calls.

items.description: `whenType` skips unification when the running `result` is T_UNIT (`if (result == T_UNIT) branchType else unifyBranches`), so `when (x) { A -> Unit; B -> "s" }` types as String — kotlinc would join the arms to a common supertype (Any-ish) and a Unit arm is not special.
items.suggestion: Treat a Unit arm like any other arm in unifyBranches (or flag an Int/String arm mixing with Unit as a Bad surface result).

items.description: The guest parser recurses unboundedly on nesting (parseElvis is right-recursive: Elvis(left, parseElvis(), ...); parenthesized expressions, blocks, types, and `${...}` template embeddings in Lexer.scanEmbedded also nest) — a deeply nested guest source raises StackOverflowError during admission, and Driver.main has no catch, so admission crashes the driver instead of reporting rejected.
items.suggestion: Track parse depth (or template/paren nesting depth) and raise a syntax diagnostic past a bound, or catch StackOverflowError at the driver boundary and report rejected.

items.description: deduplicated builds via an O(n^2) membership scan.
items.suggestion: Dedup with a LinkedHashSet.

items.description: Equality over collections zips lists and builds a per-entry HashSet comparison, adding O(n) allocation per equality check.
items.suggestion: Short-circuit elementwise comparison without auxiliary sets.

items.description: list_of_value is non-tail-recursive over spine length.
items.suggestion: Make it tail-recursive with an accumulator.

items.description: The 1,550-LOC independent reference evaluator (own eval, pattern matcher, query and register-machine models) is exercised only via the 16 non-core conformance cases — no direct unit tests, so the oracle's correctness rests solely on agreement with the engines it grades.
items.suggestion: Add focused tests pinning reference-model semantics independently of the teaching engines (Machine_model decoder, query answer ordering, lazy effect accounting).

items.description: facts/seen grow with `xs @ [x]` appends, copying the accumulated list per insert (O(n^2) over facts).
items.suggestion: Accumulate by consing and reverse once, or use a Set/Hashtbl.

items.description: The OCaml reference models share Constructor_data (fixture literal parser), Env, Prelude, Ast and Value with the teaching engines rather than reimplementing them.
items.suggestion: No change needed — see falsePositiveReason.
items.falsePositiveReason: The independence boundary covers the engine under test (eval/apply, machine execution, qeval): each model implements its own evaluator/interpreter and shares only data-language vocabulary — the same accepted boundary as TypeScript's shared AST and Kotlin's shared Admission/GValue.

items.description: reference_holds' Pythagorean arm computes 'aa + bb' with a raw + while the teaching try_holds uses checked_add; with operands above ~3e9 the debug build panics (release wraps), crashing the reference driver instead of failing the guard — a duplicated-but-divergent arithmetic path in an 'independent' oracle. Latent: corpus ranges cap at 12.
items.suggestion: Use aa.checked_add(bb) == Some(cc) to mirror the teaching arm's checked arithmetic.
items.resolution: g8 i71 normalized all holds/reference_holds predicate arithmetic to checked ops

items.description: relation_stream scans and clones every matching assertion plus the frame/args per subgoal.
items.suggestion: Index assertions by head symbol and share frames rather than cloning.

items.description: relation_arguments deep-clones each rule head per candidate application.
items.suggestion: Rename variables over a borrowed head or intern renamed copies once per rule application.

items.description: Closure bodies are deep-cloned once per closure creation and again per apply.
items.suggestion: Wrap bodies in Arc so both creation and apply share.
items.resolution: FunDef.body Arc change removed the per-creation and per-apply deep clones

items.description: `TypeKind::Zip` is absent from the `next`/`enumerate` receiver kinds, so `zip.next()` and `it.zip(w).enumerate()` are rejected as outside the allowlist though the grammar admits iterator chains "possibly chained through next, enumerate, zip" — host-valid programs are under-admitted.
items.suggestion: Include TypeKind::Zip in the receiver sets for "next" and "enumerate" (and "zip" if zipped iterators may chain further).

items.description: `&str` ordering (`a < b` on string slices) is rejected via `Diag::type_error` — the grammar's rejection taxonomy requires `Diag::unsupported` for host-valid-but-excluded constructs (§6), so the diagnostic class is mislabeled for a host-valid program.
items.suggestion: Emit Diag::unsupported for &str ordering (host-valid but outside the subset) rather than a type error.

items.description: `FnCtx.slots` is incremented at line 256 but never read — `frame_slots` is computed independently as `next_bind - bind_base`; the field is dead state carried through every function check.
items.suggestion: Remove the field or assert it equals the computed frame_slots (cheap consistency check).

items.description: check_pattern peels only one `Ref` layer, so `match &&opt { Some(..) => }` is rejected while rustc's match ergonomics read through every layer (the ops-side match_through_ref already handles multi-level reads) — under-admission of host-valid code.
items.suggestion: Loop the ref peel (or recurse) in check_pattern until a non-Ref scrutinee remains, matching the runtime's match_through_ref.

items.description: 35 admitted/rejected cases kind-assert only DiagKind::Type and DiagKind::Ownership across ~131 `Err(Diag::...)` sites in the ~5,700-LOC checker; DiagKind::Syntax is never asserted and Unsupported only via the 3 witness_classes tests, leaving most individual rejection rules unpinned.
items.suggestion: Assert DiagKind::Syntax on unparseable input and add representative per-rule cases for the largest unchecked clusters in check/expr.rs.

items.description: check_item_derives verifies fields implement PartialEq only for Eq — `#[derive(Hash)]` on a type with a non-Hash field (e.g. a HashMap field) is admitted though rustc rejects the derived impl.
items.suggestion: Apply the same field-level `implements(Hash)` check for the Hash derive as Eq/PartialEq.

items.description: List walks / projection and key conversion traverse pairs without cycle detection, so a cyclic pair (constructible via set-cdr!) hangs or overflows instead of erroring.
items.suggestion: Bound traversal or track visited addresses during list walks.

items.description: Top-level manifest_sha256 and baseline_commit are never verified by tools/host_conformance_check.py (its only sha256 use is per-case report metadata), so the recorded provenance claims are dead metadata that can drift silently from the cases on disk.
items.suggestion: Verify manifest_sha256 against the loaded cases bytes at harness startup (and baseline_commit against the git rev), or remove the fields.

items.description: Kotlin machine cases use different inputs than other editions under the same case ids (01/04 use a=1071,b=462; OCaml/TypeScript/Rust use a=206,b=40; factorial n=5 vs 6; fibonacci n=7 vs 10/8/6).
items.suggestion: No change needed — see falsePositiveReason.
items.falsePositiveReason: Per-edition divergence is contract-permitted: the oracle is per-edition (engine vs reference/native within one edition), and nothing in the plan or cases.json pins shared inputs across editions.

items.description: The section 8.2 negative witnesses (bad-nonboolean-cond, bad-nullable-cond, bad-val-reassign, and one more) are explicitly documented 'gate rejection UNRUN', and no Kotlin test exercises them — GuestAdmissionTest covers only declaration-shape rejections — so the admission gate's core host-invalid rejections are unverified anywhere, unlike Rust whose borrow-error/raw-pointer witnesses are pinned by witness_classes.rs.
items.suggestion: Add the four section-8.2 witnesses as negative admission tests asserting Admission.admit rejects each (asserting the category, not the wording).

items.description: `native_compile` invokes `rustc +1.98.1`, which requires rustc on PATH to be a rustup shim — on a host where rustc is a direct binary (system package, no rustup) the flag is treated as a filename and the check errors.
items.suggestion: No change needed where rustup provides shims (CI/dev docs assume rustup); document the assumption or invoke `rustup run 1.98.1 rustc` for robustness.
items.falsePositiveReason: rustc +toolchain is valid rustup-proxy syntax, and both CI and the documented setup install via rustup, so the shim is always in place.

items.description: The 4-line column-header comment block is repeated before every one of the 39 case rows (~273 comment lines where the other editions' manifests use 2–7 lines) — generated duplication that obscures the actual manifest rows.
items.suggestion: Emit the header once at the top of the file like the kotlin/typescript/ocaml manifests.

items.description: The only tools/*.py without a matching test file: the aspect-ratio width decision, pdfinfo parsing, and the mtime/diff-scope guardrails are unverified (manual sweep tool with --check/--apply, not a CI gate).
items.suggestion: Add a fixture test pinning the width decision and guardrail behavior, or document the script as manual-only so its untested status is explicit.

items.description: main() returns 0 unconditionally: `--check` mode reports overflowing/unresolvable figures but always exits 0, and `--apply` exits 0 even when edits are deferred or a scope violation is reported — would silently pass if ever wired as a gate.
items.suggestion: If the contract is 'report only', fine; otherwise return 1 when targets/unresolvable/deferred are nonzero.
items.falsePositiveReason: It is a manual maintenance sweep, not a gate: nothing in justfile/CI invokes it, and its docstring defines --check as report-only, so exit 0 is intended behavior today.

items.description: evalOperands/evalExpressions/evalFields accumulate [...collected, v] per element and #deferred.shift() removes the head per step, both O(n) per element.
items.suggestion: push into a mutable list and dequeue by index instead of shift.

items.description: The grammar (§1.1) requires every non-empty switch case body to complete abruptly, but the switch arm only recurses into a shared scope — the final clause is never checked, so `switch (x) { case 1: f(); }` is admitted though the contract says such a body is rejected (tsc's noFallthroughCasesInSwitch does not cover the last clause).
items.suggestion: Verify abrupt completion for the final non-empty clause (and each non-final one, rather than relying solely on noFallthrough).

items.description: `checkMemberWrite` looks up readonly fields only when the receiver is an annotated variable — `a.b.f = 1` (where `b`'s field is readonly) and any write on an unannotated receiver skip the check — though the pinned tsc still rejects, so the gap is diagnostic coverage, not admission.
items.suggestion: Track readonly-ness through member chains (or rely on tsc and drop the partial local check).
items.falsePositiveReason: The pinned tsc layer still rejects readonly writes, so no host-invalid program is admitted; the local check is belt-and-suspenders whose narrower coverage only changes which diagnostic layer reports the error.

items.description: The 1,428-LOC subset parser is covered by a single 41-line test file with 4 import-focused cases; ReadError rejection paths are exercised by roughly one exercise-level test, so most grammar exclusions are unpinned at unit level.
items.suggestion: Add negative parse cases per ReadError kind for the grammar's excluded forms (unbraced imports are the only ones covered today).

items.description: #isArrowAhead/#typeThenArrow scan tokens forward to the matching ')' or '=>' at each '(' and param ':', so deeply nested parens/types re-scan suffixes quadratically.
items.suggestion: Precompute a matching-bracket table once or bound the lookahead.

items.description: #scanNumber stores value: Number(text) on text scanned char-by-char; inputs like `1e+` or `1e` (exponent marker consumed, no digits) yield a `number` token whose value is NaN — a malformed literal admitted as a number instead of an `invalid` token.
items.suggestion: Validate the scanned text against the decimal-literal grammar (digits [.] digits [e[+-]digits]) before pushing a number token; emit `invalid` otherwise.

items.description: #scanHexEscape computes code = code*16 + parseInt(c, 16) on unvalidated characters — \x or \u followed by non-hex digits produces NaN and String.fromCharCode(NaN) silently yields '\0', so the lexer accepts escapes host semantics would reject (normally masked because admitSource's tsc layer flags it, but the lexer's own output is wrong).
items.suggestion: Check each character is a hex digit before accumulating; emit an `invalid` token on malformed hex escapes.

items.description: #scanUnicodeEscape returns String.fromCodePoint(parseInt(digits, 16)) with no validation: a guest source containing \u{...} with non-hex digits (parseInt → NaN) or a value > 0x10FFFF throws RangeError inside the lexer — an uncaught exception that crashes the driver instead of yielding an `invalid` token.
items.suggestion: Validate the hex digits and code-point range; push an `invalid` token (e.g. construct "bad-unicode-escape") instead of calling fromCodePoint on unvalidated input.

items.description: The admission workspace writes only `guest.ts` under `include: ["*.ts"]`, so a guest `import { x } from "./other.ts"` — which the grammar permits for "edition-local typed modules" — always fails with a host TS2307 module-not-found; the imports clause is unexercisable through admitSource.
items.suggestion: Either reject relative imports as UnsupportedSyntax in the subset checker, or stage the referenced edition-local units beside guest.ts.

items.description: The compiled adjoin-arg operation copies the argl array per argument, making each call's argument assembly O(k^2).
items.suggestion: append into a mutable argl register.

items.description: Query/machine .mts artifacts bypass the admission checker entirely (dynamic import of the copied module via importCase); source.ts units go through admitSource but data modules do not.
items.suggestion: No change needed — see falsePositiveReason.
items.falsePositiveReason: Contract-intended: query/machine artifacts are native TypeScript data modules, not guest source; the harness still type-checks every .mts via native_compile (host_conformance_check.py:272-282), so nothing admits unchecked code.

lowDebt.description: All seven `astral-sh/setup-uv` uses omit `version:`, so the uv binary itself installs 'latest' on every run — a floating tool version that can change gate behavior or break all jobs at once, unlike every other action/tool in this workflow which is pinned.
lowDebt.suggestion: Pin uv: `with: version: "<exact>"`.

lowDebt.description: CI gate commands drift from the canonical gate table (docs/plan/technical-modern-sicp-editions.md): rust clippy/nextest/test drop `--locked` (the same file's conformance driver.json uses it), and the ocaml step runs `dune build @check` instead of the declared `dune build`, so link-level failures the canonical gate would catch are invisible to CI. The adjacent `dune fmt --check 2>/dev/null || dune build @fmt` also hides a genuine fmt crash behind stderr suppression.
lowDebt.suggestion: Align CI commands with the declared canonical commands (`--locked` flags, `dune build`), or update the table so `just` and CI cannot diverge.

lowDebt.description: Every `uv run --project tools ...` invocation (and the justfile recipes it mirrors) runs without `--locked`/`--frozen`, so a stale or edited tools/uv.lock is silently re-locked to the newest compatible versions instead of failing — an unpinned-deps path inside otherwise frozen installs.
lowDebt.suggestion: Run the gates with `uv run --locked --project tools` (or add `uv lock --check`) so lock drift fails loudly.

lowDebt.description: Site assembly copies `$lang-sicp.pdf` with `|| true` while the sibling epub `cp` fails loudly — a missing or failed PDF artifact is silently swallowed and the Pages deploy ships an edition without its PDF.
lowDebt.suggestion: Drop the `|| true` (or guard with an explicit `[ -f ... ]` test like the figures directory above it).

lowDebt.description: `test-conformance` prepends the hardcoded mise path `~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.21.0/bin` for the bare-`node` TypeScript driver, but on hosts without that mise install (nvm/system node) the recipe silently falls through to whatever node is on PATH — the pinned-runtime contract the comment promises is unverified.
lowDebt.suggestion: Fail fast when the pinned node is absent, or assert `node --version` == 24.21.0 before running the checker.

lowDebt.description: Each force calls sink.contents() twice, re-materializing the delayed stream contents per force.
lowDebt.suggestion: Materialize once and reuse the forced value.

lowDebt.description: Emitted C code resolves variables by walking a strcmp chain over the env list, so every variable access is O(env depth) string comparisons.
lowDebt.suggestion: Emit indexed slots or a small per-frame table instead of strcmp walking.

lowDebt.description: Emitted method dispatch walks the method list linearly per call.
lowDebt.suggestion: Emit a dispatch table indexed by method id.

lowDebt.description: Driver.escape omits control characters below 0x20 other than \n \r \t, so a transcript containing e.g. \u000b or NUL produces invalid JSON and the harness's one-object parse fails as a generic driver failure. Rust's sicp-machine escapes the same range via \uXXXX; latent because no corpus transcript emits control characters.
lowDebt.suggestion: Escape every ch < 0x20 as \u%04x (matching the Rust driver) so the emitted observation stays valid JSON for arbitrary transcripts.

lowDebt.description: The native oracle reconstructs the K2JVMCompiler classpath by hardcoding its dependency versions (kotlin-reflect 1.6.10, kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm 1.8.0, annotations 23.0.0 alongside the 2.4.20 artifacts) and selects the stdlib positionally via jars[2]; a Gradle resolution change (e.g. the embedded compiler bumping its own deps) makes findJar miss, collapsing every native comparison into a driver failure rather than a case defect.
lowDebt.suggestion: Resolve the oracle classpath from Gradle itself (a task printing the resolved runtime classpath for the compiler configuration) instead of duplicating version literals and list positions.

lowDebt.description: MachineModel privately re-implements the .machine line-protocol parser (a second parser beside Driver.MachineScript) and caps execution at a 1,000,000-step guard while the teaching Machine.run() has no bound; both paths are exercised only by the 4 corpus .machine files, so parser divergence on unexercised line forms or a non-terminating program is unguarded.
lowDebt.suggestion: Share one line-protocol parser between driver and reference model (or add parser-equivalence tests), and align the termination policy between teaching and reference machines.

lowDebt.description: modeOf/compose over LAZY/SEARCH/QUERY/QUERY_LAZY/QUERY_SEARCH and the UnsupportedComposition rejection have no unit tests — every admission test uses Mode.CORE except one Mode.QUERY call; the non-CORE modes are reachable only through positively-admitted corpus programs.
lowDebt.suggestion: Table-test module-set composition, including the LAZY+SEARCH combination that must reject with UnsupportedComposition.

lowDebt.description: walkTailExpression's `else -> {}` arm misses self-calls inside StringTemplate fragments, Index, and Member receivers, so `tailrec fun f(n) = "${f(n-1)}"` (a recursive call in a non-tail interpolation) is admitted though Kotlin's tailrec requires the self-call to be in tail position.
lowDebt.suggestion: Walk StringTemplate fragments, Index/Member receivers, and any other expression nodes that can contain calls.

lowDebt.description: `whenType` skips unification when the running `result` is T_UNIT (`if (result == T_UNIT) branchType else unifyBranches`), so `when (x) { A -> Unit; B -> "s" }` types as String — kotlinc would join the arms to a common supertype (Any-ish) and a Unit arm is not special.
lowDebt.suggestion: Treat a Unit arm like any other arm in unifyBranches (or flag an Int/String arm mixing with Unit as a Bad surface result).

lowDebt.description: The guest parser recurses unboundedly on nesting (parseElvis is right-recursive: Elvis(left, parseElvis(), ...); parenthesized expressions, blocks, types, and `${...}` template embeddings in Lexer.scanEmbedded also nest) — a deeply nested guest source raises StackOverflowError during admission, and Driver.main has no catch, so admission crashes the driver instead of reporting rejected.
lowDebt.suggestion: Track parse depth (or template/paren nesting depth) and raise a syntax diagnostic past a bound, or catch StackOverflowError at the driver boundary and report rejected.

lowDebt.description: deduplicated builds via an O(n^2) membership scan.
lowDebt.suggestion: Dedup with a LinkedHashSet.

lowDebt.description: Equality over collections zips lists and builds a per-entry HashSet comparison, adding O(n) allocation per equality check.
lowDebt.suggestion: Short-circuit elementwise comparison without auxiliary sets.

lowDebt.description: list_of_value is non-tail-recursive over spine length.
lowDebt.suggestion: Make it tail-recursive with an accumulator.

lowDebt.description: The 1,550-LOC independent reference evaluator (own eval, pattern matcher, query and register-machine models) is exercised only via the 16 non-core conformance cases — no direct unit tests, so the oracle's correctness rests solely on agreement with the engines it grades.
lowDebt.suggestion: Add focused tests pinning reference-model semantics independently of the teaching engines (Machine_model decoder, query answer ordering, lazy effect accounting).

lowDebt.description: facts/seen grow with `xs @ [x]` appends, copying the accumulated list per insert (O(n^2) over facts).
lowDebt.suggestion: Accumulate by consing and reverse once, or use a Set/Hashtbl.

lowDebt.description: relation_stream scans and clones every matching assertion plus the frame/args per subgoal.
lowDebt.suggestion: Index assertions by head symbol and share frames rather than cloning.

lowDebt.description: relation_arguments deep-clones each rule head per candidate application.
lowDebt.suggestion: Rename variables over a borrowed head or intern renamed copies once per rule application.
